content:
Update, 11pm ET: Apple's System Status page shows all issues are now resolved. The original story follows below.

For the second time in a week, Apple is experiencing another major service outage affecting end users and developers. Here's what's happening.

According to Apple's System Status page, the following services are experiencing partial outages:

  • App Store: Some users affected. Users may not be able to make purchases in the iTunes Store, Mac App Store, and App Store.
  • AppleCare on Device: All users affected. AppleCare purchase service is currently unavailable.
  • iTunes Store: Some users affected. Users may not be able to make purchases in the iTunes Store, Mac App Store, and App Store.
  • Mac App Store: Some users affected. Users may not be able to make purchases in the iTunes Store, Mac App Store, and App Store.
  • Subscription Purchases: Some users affected. Users may intermittently encounter issues with this service.

All issues began at 7:40pm ET and remain unresolved. Additionally, Apple's Developer System Status page lists two ongoing issues that started at 7:20pm ET:

  • App Store – Advanced Commerce API: Some users affected. Affected services: App Store – Advanced Commerce API, App Store – In-App Purchases. We are performing emergency maintenance to improve system performance, with an estimated duration of two hours.
  • App Store – In-App Purchases: Some users affected. Affected services: App Store – Advanced Commerce API, App Store – In-App Purchases. We are performing emergency maintenance to improve system performance, with an estimated duration of two hours.

While Apple has indicated that the emergency maintenance affecting developer services will take approximately two hours, the company has not provided an estimated time to resolution for the outages directly impacting users.

We'll update this article as more information becomes available.
